newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Thames Water set for profit,div rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Thames Water set for profit,div rise.

text.p: Thames Water Plc is set to report a healthy rise in full-year profit and dividend when it announces results on Tuesday.

But it is unlikely the utility will present any special pay-outs or share buy-backs as it will be keen to avoid incurring the wrath of industry regulator Ofwat and the new Labour government, analysts said.
The regulator warned earlier this month that "excessive" pay-outs might be followed up by tougher future regulatory pricing regimes.

Industry analysts predict Thames Water will raise its dividend to 34.5 pence per share from 28.3. "We don't expect anything special. As it is, the dividend growth looks good anyway," said one industry watcher.
Pre-tax profits are expected to come in between 350 and 384 million stg compared with 228.8 million stg a year ago.
But rather than the results, investors will be more interested in what the Labour government may decide on the so-called "windfall" tax.

The government, which swept to power in a landslide victory on May 1, has vowed to impose a levy on the "excess profits" made by privatised utilities as the central plank of its first budget, due on July 2.
While it is still unclear what the windfall tax will look like, analysts do not expect Thames Water to express strong views on Tuesday.
Instead, they believe the company will focus attention on its efforts to stop leakages, while analysts will also be looking for news on Thames Water's operations abroad.

The company has one of the highest leakage rates in the country and the government promised to introduce mandatory targets for cuts in the amount of water seeping out of pipes as part of a "crisis" summit in mid-May.
Earlier this month, Thames announced it had won a 25-year contract to supply water to eastern Jakarta.
